entries.title: Psalms 91:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: He - He that makes God his habitation and refuge.

entries.title: Psalms 91:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Pestilence - From the pestilence, which like a fowler's snare takes men suddenly and unexpectedly.

entries.title: Psalms 91:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: By night - When evil accidents are most terrible and least avoidable. Arrow - The pestilence, or any such destructive calamity; such are frequently called God's arrows. By day - Thou shalt be kept from secret and open mischiefs.

entries.title: Psalms 91:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Darkness - Invisibly, so that we can neither foresee nor prevent it.

entries.title: Psalms 91:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Bear thee - Sustain or uphold thee in thy goings, as we do a child.

entries.title: Psalms 91:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The lion - Shall lie prostrate at thy feet, and thou shalt securely put thy feet upon his neck. Dragon - By which he understands all pernicious creatures, though never so strong, and all sorts of enemies.

entries.title: Psalms 91:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Because - This and the two following verses are the words of God.
